slices.basis: Singular identities derived by calendar-spine from the independently source-backed calendar publication, not from held propers. This closes fixed-calendar identity enumeration only: neither per-formulary slots, territorial additions, movable celebrations nor text coverage.

slices.basis: The complete explicitly written PC-S baseline composition queue. Formula keys identify form/cycle compositions, not additional celebrations or independently checked US-edition readings. The edition disposition expressly withholds a complete US-edition total. Every row retains unresolved target-edition correspondence.
slices.date_range: Registry kernel adopted 2026-08-22; edition dispositions retain their own evaluation dates

slices.basis: All fifty heading identities independently enumerated in the registered 2002 Ordo passage. This is the main Preface section only; proper Prefaces printed with other formularies are additional. Exact 2008/English correspondence and wording remain separate. The official 2008 variation list (Notitiae 44, printed pp. 368-380) positively names one of these appointments; that row carries established 2008 identity, with no claim of unchanged wording. The list's silence establishes nothing for the other rows, whose 2008 correspondence remains unresolved.
slices.date_range: Historical edition snapshot; no civil-year occurrence claim

slices.basis: Enumerated option identities from the source-backed sequence inventory, including options not represented by current selectors. This is an option inventory, not a count of text blocks or all ritual actions. The four main Eucharistic Prayers do not exhaust the supplementary prayers.
slices.date_range: Historical edition snapshot; no civil-year occurrence claim

slices.basis: Leaf heading identities read in the 2002 Index generalis, artifact pp. 823-824. Several headings contain multiple numbered formularies in the body; these are section targets, not asserted full Common-formulary enumeration. 2008 target correspondence remains unresolved.
slices.date_range: Historical edition snapshot; no civil-year occurrence claim

slices.basis: Positive rite and appendix identities established independently of held Mass rows. This bounded set prevents routine-Mass coverage from hiding nonstandard rites; it does not exhaust their internal texts or all ritual Masses.
slices.date_range: Historical edition snapshot; no civil-year occurrence claim

slices.basis: Accounting boundary for the whole target book. The positive slices elsewhere are subsets; their union is not asserted exhaustive. This slice has no invented target count.
slices.date_range: Historical edition snapshot; no civil-year occurrence claim

slices.basis: All sixty body-numbered full formularies beneath the thirty-three Common leaf headings, artifact pp. 536-593. Each printed numbered form is one identity; internal alternatives and its individual semantic slots are not multiplied into assembled combinations. This enumerates the registered secondary 2002 witness section only; target-2008 correspondence remains unresolved.
slices.date_range: Historical edition snapshot; no civil-year occurrence claim

slices.basis: All thirty-one named body entries in the ritual section, artifact pp. 593-667: twenty-eight Mass formularies, one alternative three-prayer set, and two referrals. Full forms may appoint antiphons by reference. These do not enumerate every internal blessing, intercession, Preface, option or ritual action. This enumerates the registered secondary 2002 witness section only; target-2008 correspondence remains unresolved.
slices.date_range: Historical edition snapshot; no civil-year occurrence claim

slices.basis: All nineteen numbered votive categories expanded through their named subdivisions, artifact pp. 724-749: twenty-three explicit Mass forms and one seasonal Marian Common referral. Optional referrals are not multiplied into guessed combinations. This enumerates the registered secondary 2002 witness section only; target-2008 correspondence remains unresolved.
slices.date_range: Historical edition snapshot; no civil-year occurrence claim

slices.basis: All named forms, prayer sets and collect categories in the dead section, artifact pp. 750-777: sixteen Mass forms, twenty three-prayer sets and six collect-only categories. Forty-two entries do not mean forty-two Masses; interchange rubrics do not define a finite Cartesian universe. This enumerates the registered secondary 2002 witness section only; target-2008 correspondence remains unresolved.
slices.date_range: Historical edition snapshot; no civil-year occurrence claim

slices.basis: All forty-nine numbered various-needs categories expanded through named subdivisions, artifact pp. 667-724: forty-nine antiphon-bearing forms, ten three-prayer sets, nine single-Collect categories and one two-Collect choice category. Sixty-nine entries are not sixty-nine full Masses. This enumerates the registered secondary 2002 witness section only; target-2008 correspondence remains unresolved.
slices.date_range: Historical edition snapshot; no civil-year occurrence claim

slices.basis: All explicit printed options in the five core proper roles of the sixty Common forms, plus their thirteen explicit Preface appointments: 94 entrance antiphons, 78 Collects, 63 offering prayers, 93 Communion antiphons, 62 postcommunions and 13 Preface appointments. The 403 entries are contextual appointments, not 403 distinct texts or assembled Masses. References and applicability follow their source loci; unprinted/general-rubric appointments, additional Preface choices within a reference and exact 2008 correspondence remain unresolved. The official 2008 variation list (Notitiae 44, printed pp. 368-380) positively names nine of these appointments; those rows carry established 2008 identity, with no claim of unchanged wording. The list's silence establishes nothing for the other rows, whose 2008 correspondence remains unresolved.
slices.date_range: Historical edition snapshot; no civil-year occurrence claim

slices.basis: All 20 numbered entries in the main Ordo Solemn blessings section of the 2002 source, artifact pp. 370-383. This does not include proper blessings printed with ritual Masses or prayers over the people appointed elsewhere. Exact 2008 correspondence remains unresolved.
slices.date_range: Historical edition snapshot; no civil-year occurrence claim

slices.basis: All 28 numbered entries in the main Ordo Prayers over the people section of the 2002 source, artifact pp. 370-383. This does not include proper blessings printed with ritual Masses or prayers over the people appointed elsewhere. Exact 2008 correspondence remains unresolved.
slices.date_range: Historical edition snapshot; no civil-year occurrence claim

slices.basis: Positive source-defined appointments throughout the official 2008 Supplementum, printed pp. 380-387: extended Pentecost Vigil with its two openings, readings/responses/prayers, conditional Vespers actions and explicit referrals; two Super oblata appointments; three memorial Collects and four Common referrals. The three general dismissal additions are already owned by the main Ordinary-option slice and are not duplicated. This closes the published supplement at appointment/referral granularity, not every downstream text in the Missal, Lectionary or Hours. Identities are established by the 2008 publication itself.
slices.date_range: Historical edition snapshot; no civil-year occurrence claim

slices.basis: Forty-eight positive 2002 source structures: eleven index-only chant categories, three rites, four water/salt prayer options, eight sprinkling chants, eleven sample universal-prayer sets, four preparation units and seven thanksgiving units. Appendix I music is absent from the accessible text body; named index categories do not enumerate every musical option. Three children's Eucharistic Prayers are separately excluded from the target 2008 book and never entered as targets.
slices.date_range: Historical edition snapshot; no civil-year occurrence claim

slices.basis: Six source-named supplementary Eucharistic-Prayer forms, Reconciliation I-II and Various Needs I-IV, artifact pp. 389-414. These refine the earlier rite-level identities and do not multiply Mass formularies. Internal options, proper Prefaces and exact 2008 correspondence remain separate.
slices.date_range: Historical edition snapshot; no civil-year occurrence claim

slices.basis: The single-minister Order of Mass as one source-named form, artifact pp. 383-389; its thirty-four numbered units are not individually inventoried by this form row. This refines the earlier rite-level identity.
slices.date_range: Historical edition snapshot; no civil-year occurrence claim

slices.basis: 185 named Mass formularies in the 2002 secondary digital temporal body, artifact pp. 82–303, web L4047–12305. Form headings and surrounding rubrics, not a reconstructed civil calendar or held corpus, control membership. Conditional collect and Gospel-component variants do not multiply the base formularies. Exact 2008/English correspondence remains unresolved.
slices.date_range: 2002 source witness; 2008/English target correspondence unresolved

slices.basis: 19 positive temporal referrals or conditional appointments; bounded supplementary enumeration, not every rubric or repeated Ordinary reference. Seven Preface appointments redirect elsewhere and are not newly owned temporal Prefaces.
slices.date_range: 2002 source witness; 2008/English target correspondence unresolved

slices.basis: 58 positive exceptional rite, rite-unit and prayer-set identities in the temporal body. These have distinct granularity and do not add to the Mass-form count. Internal ritual texts, alternatives and slots are not exhaustively enumerated.
slices.date_range: 2002 source witness; 2008/English target correspondence unresolved

slices.basis: Forty-six additional appointments in the full 2002 Preface index after excluding the fifty already enumerated main-section entries and two exact repeated index referrals. The full index has ninety-eight contextual entries; ninety-six remain after those explicit referral duplicates. This is source index membership, not a claim of ninety-six unique formula wordings. The official 2008 variation list (Notitiae 44, printed pp. 368-380) positively names one of these appointments; that row carries established 2008 identity, with no claim of unchanged wording. The list's silence establishes nothing for the other rows, whose 2008 correspondence remains unresolved.
slices.date_range: Historical edition snapshot; no civil-year occurrence claim

slices.basis: All 212 named Mass-proper entries in the 2002 Proper of Saints body, artifact pp. 415-535: 85 forms with five printed core proper roles, 6 three-prayer sets, 121 own-Collect categories. The 207 celebration headings expand three vigil/day pairs and All Souls 1-3. This is distinct from the source-calendar identity slice and from complete Masses including readings/Ordinary. Exact 2008 correspondence remains unresolved.
slices.date_range: Historical edition snapshot; no civil-year occurrence claim

slices.basis: Thirty explicitly printed Preface referrals in the Proper of Saints. These appoint other owned Prefaces and do not add thirty new Preface bodies. Only this source referral class is enumerated; Common and seasonal choice combinations remain separate. Exact 2008 correspondence remains unresolved.
slices.date_range: Historical edition snapshot; no civil-year occurrence claim

slices.basis: Six positive Presentation-rite structures: procession and solemn-entrance forms, two candle-blessing prayers, two numbered procession chants. The initial chant referral and other suitable-chant permission are not exhausted by the numbered chant options. Exact 2008 correspondence remains unresolved.
slices.date_range: Historical edition snapshot; no civil-year occurrence claim

slices.basis: All 564 explicit printed core-role headings beneath the 212 sanctoral entries: 85 five-role forms plus 6 three-prayer sets plus 121 own Collects. These identify source role appointments, not every alternative under a heading and not imported Common/seasonal slots. Every marker was extracted independently from the source body; the final form locator retains the exact web line and distinguishes the form opening artifact page from the slot location. Exact 2008 correspondence remains unresolved. The official 2008 variation list (Notitiae 44, printed pp. 368-380) positively names ten of these appointments; those rows carry established 2008 identity, with no claim of unchanged wording. The list's silence establishes nothing for the other rows, whose 2008 correspondence remains unresolved.
slices.date_range: Historical edition snapshot; no civil-year occurrence claim

slices.basis: Every leaf heading the selected U.S. edition's General Index (printed pp. 5*-8*) lists under the Proper of Time, the Order of Mass with a single minister, the Appendix to the Order of Mass, the Commons, Ritual Masses, Masses and Prayers for Various Needs and Occasions, Votive Masses, Masses for the Dead, and the Appendices with Preparation and Thanksgiving: 210 headings, each image-checked. A parent heading counts only through its children when it has no page of its own or shares its first child's page (the dedication anniversary, the Scrutinies); needs categories 7 and 13 have their own pages and count beside their anniversary children. Kinds are the nearest permitted kind for a heading, not a granularity claim: 20 of the 41 temporal 'celebration' headings group a Sunday with its week, a run of weekdays or a whole season. Ritual, needs, votive and dead Mass headings are recorded as 'form', the kind the 2002 body slices give those sections, although one may hold several forms, a prayer set or a Collect only. Front-matter documents, the main Order of Mass section, the Proper of Saints month headings and the two further indexes are outside these targets and stated as boundaries. U.S. recension only: these headings do not duplicate, replace or reconcile the 184 PC-S composition keys of postconciliar-temporal-composition-registry, and they assert no correspondence to the Latin 2002/2008 slices, including the 33 Latin Common index headings. No held-row join is asserted.
slices.date_range: 2011 as printed on the edition's title page; preview PDF produced 2018-2019; no civil-year occurrence claim

slices.basis: Five source-printed antiphon alternatives at artifact p. 73 / printed p. 65, independently read in the authoritative 2010/2011 English excerpt whose foreword expressly scopes its antiphons to Missale Romanum 2002/2008. These establish only antiphon identity and appointment, not Latin wording, a complete formulary, or publication rights. Day Entrance alternatives have no distinct v1 option join and remain unresolved; the unique Vigil Entrance/Communion and Day Communion roles are joined. Compiler Graduale psalm suggestions are excluded. Extended-Vigil ritual structure belongs to its separate 2008 Supplementum slice.
slices.date_range: Historical third-typical-edition structural appointments; no civil-year or exact-wording claim

slices.basis: Eleven independently printed role headings/referrals at artifact pp. 95-96 / printed pp. 41-42: five Vigil roles and six Day roles. Each target is a headed role, not a count or complete individual join of every reading, response, cycle alternative, incipit, title, or verse. Exact candidate Mass/form/unique-role addresses are recorded where v1 can express them; all retain unresolved 2008 target correspondence because this source-local 1981 reading alone is no new certificate for the target Missal. Vigil First Reading remains unjoined rather than conflating its four source choices into one held entry.
slices.date_range: Source-local 1981 Ordo lectionum Missae nn. 62-63; target correspondence remains unresolved

slices.basis: Twelve source-local prayer and Ordinary-variable appointments read independently of held rows: three Day orations, two Vigil Collect alternatives and two other Vigil orations, Preface directions in both forms, conditional proper Communicantes directions in both forms, and Day paschal dismissal. Antiphons are owned by the stronger positive 2002/2008 excerpt slice. Source presence does not establish 2008 target correspondence or word-exactness. Existing model addresses are retained where available; no Communicantes option identity is invented. Gloria/Creed, optional solemn blessings, invariant Ordinary, ceremonial actions, cycle variants and the separate 2008 extended Vigil are outside this partial text-slot scope.
slices.date_range: Registered secondary 2002 reproduction, artifact pp. 265-267; 2008 correspondence unresolved

slices.basis: Forty-five positive source role anchors:37 own Lenten weekday Prayers over the People, four AshWednesday distribution chants, three Presentation candle/procession chants and the Chrism renewal dialogue. The37 weekday forms are credited to the registered2002 body-form inventory joined to the freshly viewed general Lent rubric3, not37 new individual prayer/body collations. Eight appointments have positive structural2008 identity;36 other weekday prayers and the Chrism renewal retain unresolved target correspondence. No exact body, permission, choice-universe, whole-form or normative annual denominator is inferred.
slices.date_range: Held source2002/2010 and bounded official2008 appointment evidence; no civil-year or enacted-use claim

This is a finite partial module for the extended Pentecost Vigil: the before-reading Collect, four ordered Old Testament readings and corresponding prayers, after-Gloria Collect, and Romans 8:22-27 continuation are represented. Six after-reading prayer options occupy four prayer seats, with three mutually exclusive options after Ezekiel. The opening admits either Vespers joined to Mass or the usual Mass opening; Gloria and the second Collect follow the four Old Testament readings. The special Ordinary frame, the optional replacement of psalmody with silence, and the unselected Vespers branches remain unmodeled. The Lectionary readings are appointed ad libitum: this records the source order, not an obligation to use all four. Reading-omission pathways remain unmodeled.

translations.caution:
A LITERARY TRANSLATION, CHOSEN AS A VOICE. Caswall, Neale, Aylward and Bute
differ materially over these five texts. The active overlay records the
maintainer's choice of Caswall as the through-line across the relevant texts;
it does not argue that Caswall is right.

The English is metrical verse and is not a clause-for-clause rendering. Where the
Latin sets a short strophe Caswall may fold two into one six-line stanza, and the
stanza divisions in the text recorded here are his and not the Missal's. He
renders no Amen and no Alleluia anywhere: every one of these five propers ends in
the Latin with an acclamation that the English simply does not have.
